subject: Billing matrix: token accounting, context length, and minimums — review
messages:

Cc: Mark Delaney <cfo@omnihealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify billing matrix for long-context chat and rounding

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the call yesterday. We're finalizing the procurement worksheet and need a short, unambiguous explanation of how Redwood will bill the following items so our finance team can map to our ledger:

- How are tokens counted for multi-turn chat? (do you bill input+output tokens, and is your tokenizer consistent across models?)
- When a chat uses a 60k context model but an individual call only has a 2k prompt + 600-token completion, what context-length factors into billing?
- Rounding/quantum rules: we saw references to a "quantum" in prior docs — what is it for hosted plans and for dedicated pools?
- Minimums and pilot proration: our pilot runs one month with sporadic usage — will minimums be prorated daily or monthly?

I've attached a small sample usage export (sample_usage_export.csv) with three example calls (columns: call_id, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, conversation_id) — can you walk us through how those would appear on an invoice?

We want to avoid surprises in the invoice mapping to our internal charge codes. If you can send a short worked example and any proposed SOW language for the minimum/discount mechanics, that would be ideal.

Appreciate it —
Lisa
Procurement Manager | OmniHealth
procurements@omnihealth.com

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear examples. Looping in Karthik and Vanessa: Karthik to confirm token/counting mechanics and rounding behavior, Vanessa to propose recommended minimums/discount wording for the SOW.

High-level answers so finance can start mapping (I will follow up with worked examples):
- We bill both prompt (input) and completion (output) tokens. The tokenizer is model-specific but our billing pipeline normalizes counts to the model variant listed on the invoice.
- Context length considered for billing is the actual tokens processed per call (prompt + completion). Holding a long conversation history in a customer-side session does not by itself create a higher per-call bill unless those tokens are sent to the model in that API call.
- Quantum/rounding differs by product: hosted API uses a small per-call quantum for token aggregation; dedicated customers can request a different quantum in SOW. Vanessa will propose explicit language.
- Pilot minimums: we offer prorated minimums for pilot months (pro-rated to the number of days active in the month) by default for sales-assisted pilots.

I attached an initial billing matrix draft for your team to review (redwood_billing_matrix_draft.xlsx). Karthik — can you take the CSV and produce the three-line invoice examples and include the rounding math?

Best,
Irene Choi

Hi Lisa / Irene — I ran the three sample rows through our billing logic. Below is the step-by-step and the final invoice line mapping. I kept numbers explicit so you can paste into your ledger.

Billing rules we applied for these examples (hosted API standard profile):
- Token accounting: billed_tokens = prompt_tokens + completion_tokens
- Quantum (rounding): billed tokens are rounded up to the nearest 8-token quantum per call. (Hosted default quantum = 8 tokens; Dedicated customers may specify 4 or 16 via SOW.)
- Minimum per-line: no per-call minimum beyond quantum. Monthly minimums are applied at the account level (see Vanessa's note).
- Context length: the "model max context" (e.g., 60k) is a capability, not a per-call multiplier. We bill only the tokens transmitted in that call.

Worked examples (values from your CSV):
1) call_id: C-101 | model: rwd-60k | prompt_tokens: 2000 | completion_tokens: 600
   billed_tokens_pre_round = 2000 + 600 = 2600
   quantum = 8 -> 2600 / 8 = 325.0 -> rounded up = 325 -> billed_tokens = 325 * 8 = 2600 (no change)
   invoice line: rwd-60k | 2600 tokens | unit price $0.0006/token | line total $1.56

2) call_id: C-102 | model: rwd-60k | prompt_tokens: 120 | completion_tokens: 31
   billed_tokens_pre_round = 151
   quantum = 8 -> 151 / 8 = 18.875 -> rounded up = 19 -> billed_tokens = 19 * 8 = 152
   invoice line: rwd-60k | 152 tokens | unit price $0.0006/token | line total $0.0912

3) call_id: C-103 | model: rwd-16k | prompt_tokens: 6400 | completion_tokens: 1280
   billed_tokens_pre_round = 7680
   quantum = 8 -> 7680 / 8 = 960 -> billed_tokens = 7680
   invoice line: rwd-16k | 7680 tokens | unit price $0.00055/token (16k model price) | line total $4.224

Notes on KV/prefix caching: if a call reuses a cached prefix server-side (same conversation_id and within cache TTL), we subtract the cached prefix tokens from the prompt_tokens before applying the quantum. That reduces billed_tokens for repeated system/context messages. For your CSV none of the conversation_id values matched cached prefixes, so no cache reduction applied.

If you'd like, I can produce a CSV-formatted invoice sample mapping call_ids to invoice lines (with rounding math columns).

-Karthik
Sr. Applied ML Engineer (Inference Accounting) | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify billing matrix for long-context chat and rounding — commercial proposal

Hi Lisa / Mark — thanks to Karthik and Irene for the worked examples. Commercial follow-up with a compact SOW proposal and an ask for a one-time pilot concession: 

Proposal summary (short):
- Monthly committed minimum: 50,000 billed tokens / month (billed at $0.00055/token).
- Pilot month: prorated minimum = 50,000 * (days active / calendar days). For a 10-day pilot the minimum would be 16,129 tokens (rounded up to the nearest 1,000 for billing simplicity).
- Volume discount: 15% off unit price at or above the committed minimum for months 2-12.
- Quantum: hosted default quantum = 8 tokens; dedicated pool quantum can be negotiated in the SOW (we can set to 4 tokens for a 12-month commitment).
- Cache credits: we will credit prefix/KV cache reuse token savings on the invoice as a separate negative line item to make reconciliation straightforward.

SOW wording I recommend including (summary for procurement):
"Monthly commitment and proration: Customer agrees to a monthly committed billed-token minimum. For the initial partial month, the committed minimum will be prorated by calendar days active and rounded to the nearest 1,000 tokens for invoice presentation. Volume discounts apply to billed tokens above the minimum as specified in the rate table."

Attachments: I attached a draft SOW and a one-page fee table to sign. If OmniHealth confirms the 50k minimum and 15% volume discount, we will issue a final quote and a DocuSign SOW.

Two quick asks for Mark (cc'd):
1) Can your team accept the rounding-to-1,000 convenience rule for pilot proration? It significantly reduces invoice noise.
2) If OmniHealth prefers strict prorate without rounding, we can do that but need a short approval path for an exceptions worksheet.

If you confirm, I’ll circulate the final DocuSign link today.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
